subject: Medilume SOW: backstop clause, capacity uplift, and rate rebalance
messages:
From: Ellie Rogers <ellie.rogers@medilume.com>
To: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medilume.com
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SOW edits + capacity uplift for Q3

Markus —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We had a quick internal alignment and have two requests so we can move forward with procurement this quarter:

1) Add a 15% burst capacity buffer to the Order Form (exhibit B) for Q3 (anticipated traffic spike for pilot).
2) A short-term price rebalance: hold the current unit fee for incremental burst usage through the end of Q3, then revert to the standard tiered rates unless we agree a longer contract.

Procurement asked if you can provide:
- A redlined SOW showing the exhibit change + a short explanatory note outlining the commercial backstop (how the price hold will be applied and for how long).
- Confirmation of any SLA/acceptance changes tied to the burst capacity.
- A target timeline — we need final docs in Hand by 2026-05-21 to route for internal approval.

I attached the RFQ and current internal timeline (RFQ_Medilume_capacity_schedule.xlsx). Happy to hop on a brief call if helpful.

Thanks,
Ellie Rogers
Director, Cloud Integrations
Medilume Health

From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-05-17T12:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: SOW edits + capacity uplift for Q3

Markus / Steph —

Attached: Medilume_SOW_v3_redline.pdf (redline of Exhibit B + new Exhibit G: "Burst Capacity Backstop"). Key legal points I recommend:

- Timeboxed Price Hold: A one-time temporary price hold for incremental burst units through 2026-09-30. After that date, pricing defaults to the standard tiered fee schedule unless parties agree in writing.
- Measurement Clause: Define "incremental burst units" as tokens consumed above the baseline monthly committed throughput; include a worked example.
- Backstop Cap: Cap the total value of the price-hold benefit to 150% of the average monthly baseline to control exposure.
- Rollback / Reconciliation: Include a 30-day reconciliation window post-Q3 to reconcile actual usage and apply pro rata charges/credits.
- SLA note: burst capacity is provided best-effort within the burst pool; we should avoid promising lower p95 latency during tiered burst. Suggested language included in the redline.

If you want a slightly more customer-friendly commercial (higher cap or longer hold), tell me the specific parameters and I'll prepare alternative language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
attachments: Medilume_SOW_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)

From: Ellie Rogers <ellie.rogers@medilume.com>
To: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medilume.com
Date: 2026-05-18T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Medilume SOW: backstop clause, capacity uplift, and rate rebalance

Thanks, Laura and Markus —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the redline. A couple of procurement items to flag:

- The backstop cap at 150% is acceptable, but procurement would prefer the reconciliation window to be 45 days to align with our billing cycle.
- We need the price-hold to be explicitly applied to any overage charges (not to committed baseline). Please confirm the worked example covers this.
- Our procurement team requires a short vendor data-processing addendum reference in the SOW (not a full DPA) that points to the existing DPA we signed last year. I've attached our standard procurement terms for reference (Medilume_Procurement_Terms.pdf).

If you can send the redlined Order Form + a minor amendment (one-page) that procurement can sign and return, we can aim to get approvals by 2026-05-21.

Thanks — happy to take a 15-minute call if it speeds things up.

Ellie
attachments: Medilume_Procurement_Terms.pdf (pdf)
